Form fields are reconstructed from statements in the source document; the derived competitive set and the expected conclusion are taken from it directly. The per-dimension expected levels are an ASSISTANT MAPPING of that conclusion onto the six calibrated dimensions - they are not a recorded client label. The BAND, not the dimension vector, is the bar (spec 10.6).
_meta.expected_conclusion: Market real, position open, but the demand side is unbuilt (spec 10.1)
_meta.notes: 534 listings, 18 categories, #1 on Google for 'pet directory singapore', transparent S$19-29/mo pricing. The supply side is built and the demand side is not: '534 listings x 0 visitors = 0 value delivered'. Market is SGD 412M and growing; nobody owns 'the trusted full-service pet directory'.

form.category: Online business directory for pet services in Singapore - grooming, veterinary, boarding, retail, pet food and beverage, funeral services and more, across 18 categories.
form.positioning_sentence: The trusted full-service directory of pet businesses in Singapore.
form.differentiator: We have the largest verified database of pet businesses in Singapore - 534 listings across 18 categories - and we rank first on Google for the category's own search term. We publish our pricing openly at S$19-29 a month where competitors hide it behind a contact form. We also have features no competitor has: pet obituaries, a pet showcase, and an influencer programme. Every listing is checked before it goes live.
form.undercut_on: Visitors. We have almost no traffic, so a business paying for a listing sees no return, and the paywall keeps the roughly 490 remaining licensed businesses out. A free classifieds group or a Google search does the same job at no cost.
form.your_price_point: S$19-29 per month for a listing subscription.
form.their_price_point: Google search, Facebook groups and free classifieds cost nothing.

customer_description: Singapore pet owners looking for a local pet service - grooming, vet, boarding or retail - usually searching on mobile in the moment of need. Also the pet businesses that would pay to be found.

derived_competitive_set.derivation_method: Derived from the SG pet-services discovery category: how pet owners actually find a business, and which intermediaries already own that moment.

members: asking in a WhatsApp or Facebook group
asking a friend or the vet
tier_0_default.why: Most pet-service discovery is word of mouth, not directory search.

tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: The free route is fast, familiar and already in the customer's hand.

tier_2_direct_set.why: The same job - a browsable list of pet businesses - is done by these.

tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: Google Maps and search own the discovery moment outright. A directory competes for the customer's attention against an interface that is already open on their phone.
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: The category's real incumbent is not another directory.

tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: An authoritative registry answers 'is this business licensed' better than a directory can.

members: vets and groomers recommending a business directly
tier_5_professional_route.why: A trusted professional's recommendation bypasses the directory entirely.

members: social media accounts of individual pet businesses building their own audience
tier_6_indirect.why: A business with its own following does not need a directory.

_expected.why: The market is real and the position is genuinely open - competitive room is the strongest dimension, because no directory owns 'trusted full-service' and the incumbent is Google rather than a rival directory. But the demand side is unbuilt: demand reach is the weakest dimension at 1, since the database delivers no visitors. Defensibility is weak: a listings database is a stocked asset but it is rebuildable.
